Tidy comparison of forecast scores across mvgam models

Source: R/compare_scores.R
compare_scores.Rd

Scores the forecasts of several models of the same held-out data with one rule, then stacks the results in one table for comparison. Lower scores are better. The table has one row per model, series and forecast horizon. A joint score ("energy", "variogram" or "twenergy") scores all series together. Its per-series rows hold NA. The rows with series == "all_series" hold its value.

Usage

compare_scores(..., score = "crps", model_names = NULL, score_args = list())

Arguments

...

Two or more mvgam_forecast objects from forecast.mvgam(). A named argument, as in compare_scores(GAM = fc1, AR = fc2), names its model. An unnamed one takes the expression passed, such as "fc1".

score

Character name of the scoring rule. The section 'Available scores' of score.mvgam_forecast() lists them.

model_names

Optional character vector of model names, one per forecast. It replaces the names taken from the call.

score_args

Optional named list of further arguments of score.mvgam_forecast(), such as score_args = list(interval_width = 0.6).

Value

A tibble of class mvgam_compare_scores, with columns:

  • model: a factor with one level per forecast.

  • series: a factor of series names, with an "all_series" level for a joint score.

  • eval_horizon: the forecast horizon, 1 for the first held-out time.

  • score: the value of the score.

  • in_interval: whether the observation fell in the central interval, as score.mvgam_forecast() reports it.

See also

score.mvgam_forecast(), plot.mvgam_compare_scores(), compare_elpds(), forecast.mvgam(), ensemble.mvgam_forecast()

Other forecasting: ensemble.mvgam_forecast(), forecast.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), score.mvgam_forecast()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
# Two models of one count series: a smooth of x with and without
# an AR(1) trend. The trend model samples with smaller steps
# (adapt_delta = 0.95). That avoids divergent transitions when
# lfo_cv() refits it to shorter stretches of the series
mod_gam <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), data = simdat$data_train,
                 family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 209 of 2000 (10.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
mod_ar <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
                data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
                chains = 2, silent = 2,
                control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95))
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
fc_gam <- forecast(mod_gam, newdata = simdat$data_test)
fc_ar <- forecast(mod_ar, newdata = simdat$data_test)

# One row per model and horizon, scored by the discrete ranked
# probability score (lower is better)
scores <- compare_scores(fc_gam, fc_ar, score = "drps",
                         model_names = c("GAM", "AR"))
summary(scores)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 4
#>    series   eval_horizon    GAM    AR
#>    <fct>           <int>  <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 series_1            1  2.39  1.29 
#>  2 series_1            2  2.59  1.18 
#>  3 series_1            3 10.5   6.33 
#>  4 series_1            4  7.96  5.82 
#>  5 series_1            5  8.68  4.19 
#>  6 series_1            6  4.07  2.28 
#>  7 series_1            7  0.722 0.878
#>  8 series_1            8  0.781 0.900
#>  9 series_1            9  2.73  2.03 
#> 10 series_1           10  4.58  2.71 
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# The AR model's DRPS minus the GAM's. Negative values favour the
# AR model
plot(scores, relative = "GAM")


# Next, ensemble() combines the two forecasts
# }
